_schema.note: Consumed by scripts/check_untranslated.py. Each entry records a (key, locale) pair whose translation is INTENTIONALLY identical to the en-US source, so the gate can tell 'identical on purpose' from 'nobody translated it'.
_schema.rule: Prefer translating over allowlisting. Use "*" only when the value is identical in every supported language; otherwise list the specific tags, because a key translated in 12 locales proves the other 3 are real misses.

gamevault.downloadDirPlaceholder.reason: A filesystem path and nothing else. The label that used to precede it ("Default: ") was removed at the user's request, leaving no words to translate.

deckTabs.microsoft.reason: Company name. Unchanged in every supported language.

deckTabs.gamevault.reason: Product name of the self-hosted GameVault server. It is not a descriptive phrase, and the project ships no localised name, so every locale keeps the Latin-script original — including ar-SA, which transliterates no other store name either.

storeConnections.microsoftStore.reason: Microsoft ships the storefront under this name in all these markets; every locale independently kept it.

gameInfoPanel.buttons.dlc.reason: DLC is the established loanword in these languages. Only ar-SA expands it.

gameInfoPanel.labels.metacritic.reason: Brand name plus a colon. fr-FR differs only by its spaced colon; ko/zh append a word for 'score'.

gameInfoPanel.labels.status.reason: 'Status' is the native word in German, Dutch, Polish and Brazilian Portuguese.

gameInfoPanel.labels.store.reason: 'Store' is standard German usage for a digital storefront.

unifiedLibrary.storeLabel.reason: Same word as gameInfoPanel.labels.store, kept consistent.

navigation.storesTitle.reason: German uses the English plural 'Stores' for digital storefronts.

gameInfoPanel.buttons.details.reason: 'Details' is the native word in German and Dutch.

gameInfoPanel.buttons.guides.reason: 'Guides' is the common gaming term in German and French.

gameInfoPanel.buttons.support.reason: 'Support' is the native word in German and French.

gameInfoPanel.buttons.synopsis.reason: 'Synopsis' is the native word in French and Dutch.

gameInfoPanel.buttons.discussions.reason: 'Discussions' is the French word, and matches Steam's own French UI.

gameInfoPanel.buttons.pointsShop.reason: Steam leaves 'Points Shop' untranslated in its Dutch UI.

launchLogs.filterInfo.reason: 'Info' is the native abbreviation in these four languages.

saveFolder.filterLabel.reason: 'Filter' is the native word in German and Dutch.

security.filter.label.reason: 'Filter' is the native word in German and Dutch.

cloudSave.cloud.reason: 'Cloud' is the borrowed term in German, Italian and Dutch.

cloudSave.local.reason: 'Local' is the native word in Spanish and Portuguese.

downloads.title.reason: 'Downloads' is the established plural in German, Dutch and Brazilian Portuguese.

tabs.downloads.reason: Same word as downloads.title, kept consistent.

installButton.update.reason: 'Update' is the native word in German and Dutch; shown uppercased.

gameDetailsSettings.simple.reason: 'Simple' is spelled identically in Spanish and French.

gameInfoPanel.compatibility.compatible.reason: Valve's own word for the SteamOS 'Compatible' rating is literally 'Compatible' in Spanish and 'compatible' in French (SteamOSCompatibility_Category_Compatible in the Steam client's shared_spanish / shared_french bundles). Matching Valve matters more than differing from en-US: the user sees this same word in Steam's own compatibility section. The other 13 locales do differ, which is what makes these two deliberate rather than missed.

gamevault.password.reason: Same word as ubisoftAuth.passwordLabel, kept consistent. The other 14 locales translated this key, which is why only it-IT is listed.

storeOwnership.noteCloud.reason: A one-word note on an owned Xbox chip for a title that also streams through Xbox Cloud Gaming. German, French, Italian and Dutch use the loanword 'Cloud' itself for cloud gaming (Steam's own 'Steam Cloud' is untranslated in all four); a native word ('Wolke', 'nuage', 'nuvola', 'wolk') would read as weather. The other 11 locales translate it, which is why only these four are listed.

storeOwnership.platformPc.reason: Platform name on a Steam Store ribbon chip ('Xbox · PC'). 'PC' is the term every supported language uses for Windows gaming, as Steam's own store does.

storeOwnership.platformConsole.reason: French, Italian, Dutch and Brazilian Portuguese all write 'console' for a game console; the other locales translate it.

storeOwnership.platformPcConsole.reason: 'PC' plus the word 'console', which these four languages write as English does (see storeOwnership.platformConsole).

storeOwnership.platformPlayAnywhere.reason: Microsoft's program name (Xbox Play Anywhere), shown untranslated on Microsoft's own localized store pages.

storeOwnership.noteGold.reason: Brand: Games with Gold / Xbox Live Gold. The Xbox console marks these titles with an untranslated 'GOLD' badge in every language.

auth.microsoft.code.reason: Label before the Microsoft sign-in code in the QAM. German, French and Dutch all use the word 'Code'.

storeOwnership.messageGamePass.reason: Brand name (Xbox Game Pass), unchanged on Microsoft's own localized pages.

storeOwnership.messageXboxCloud.reason: Brand name (Xbox Cloud Gaming), unchanged on Microsoft's own localized pages.
